reviews.text: To preface, this short list of system requirements outline what I'm about to say, this is here to show even the strongest of rigs may struggle to achieve. These are the system requirements on launch: MINIMUM: Processor: AMD 3600x Memory: 8 GB RAM Graphics: 1060 GTX Storage: 100 MB available space RECOMMENDED: Processor: AMD 5700x Memory: 8 GB RAM Graphics: 2070 RTX Storage: 100 MB available space This game demonstrates how graphically and computationally intensive a game can be. What we have witnessed is short of a masterpiece, pushing the fabric of what we can achieve as a society when intelligence surpasses our limitations. Created using love and devotion to the craft, Faith G has delivered on something we did not know was promised. This game does not simple raise the bar; it redefines it, setting a new gold standard for the entire industry, Elden Ring? Wukong? Baldurs Gate? Make way for the newest and strongest competitor, Idle_Colony.

I liked (the) Gnorp Analogue, but this game didn't really catch my interest in 2 hours I have played. It certainly looks good with interesting mechanics, but starting from the little simple ones, like drawing paths for your colonists, to builds you can pursue in progression tree (chopping trees, hitting moles, weather and such), they are not feeling catchy enough for me for some reason. Or maybe it is that this game throws a lot of buildings with dozens of upgrades into you right away, I certainly felt "overwhelmed" a bit, probably compared to all other incremental games I have played. At the current price in my region being higher than Gnorp's one, I am not feeling like continuing. Though would recommend it for trying out if you are fan of the genre for sure.

The "features" of this game are fighting each other harder than streamer Emiru fighting a darksouls boss.

The Review Critic: Dopamine Overload – "THE FRUIT ADDICTION" Edition Idle games. They’re the gaming equivalent of potato chips—you know exactly what you’re getting, but somehow, you still end up eating the whole bag. Enter Addicted to the Fruits (not its real name, but let’s face it, it might as well be). This game takes the idle formula, cranks up the dopamine, and hits you with a visual flair that makes counting numbers feel like a Vegas light show. Gameplay: Let’s not kid ourselves: all idle games peak the second you go from 1+1=2 to 2+2=4 and onward into exponential madness. That’s just how the genre works. But Addicted to the Fruits takes that formula and sprays it with glitter, confetti, and a dopamine cannon so powerful it should come with a warning label. The gameplay loop is as simple as they come, but the style is what sets this one apart. Watching the numbers tick up feels less like math and more like a fireworks display. It’s pure satisfaction, packaged in fruity chaos. Visual Flair: The visuals? Chef’s kiss. This game doesn’t just show you numbers climbing—it celebrates them. Each milestone feels like winning the lottery, and the colors, animations, and effects keep you glued to the screen, hypnotized by the sheer joy of progress. The Verdict: Addicted to the Fruits isn’t here to reinvent the wheel—it’s here to turn that wheel into a neon spectacle of endless entertainment. If you’ve got a soft spot for idle games and a tolerance for losing hours of your life to exponential growth, this one’s a must-play. Just watch out—your spouse might not appreciate your new obsession. 10/10, my wife is still mad, and I’m still clicking. If this review has juiced up your interest, hit that thumbs-up button and follow The Review Critic for more refreshingly honest takes. Because when it comes to idle games, I’m your enabler. The Review Critic, signing off to crunch more numbers and dodge more side-eyes from the missus.

There are so many tiny things in this extreme tiny game that makes me wonder if the dev even care about the game itself or just of the revenue. i have a strong feeling it is the 2nd. the final game still feels like a demo with only a tiny part of a real game

一款看似挂机但其实是资源配置的游戏。 初见来看这似乎是一个观察一堆蚂蚁工具人不停干活的游戏，毕竟开始时玩家能给予的干预非常有限。 然而在启用鼠标技能和路径管理后一切都变了。 路径管理允许玩家指挥采集工前往指定位置，这使得玩家可以快速形成最高效的采集路线，或者在建设时规避相关资源。 而鼠标技能则赋予了玩家鼠标额外的能力：快速砍树与快速采集，快速采集除非为了奖杯否则意义不大，而快速砍树则可以有效对场景中的资源树进行选种管理，从而提高获取高级树苗的速度。 基于这两者这款游戏将从挂机游戏变成资源配给与产业规划游戏，合理投资功能提高产能，更快的获取高级水果资源，合理分配技能点最大化生产倍率，或者挑战无工人模式和其他特定奖杯。所以熟悉之后这游戏玩起来其实挺忙的（） 总结：适合上班摸鱼

Idle Colony is a charming and surprisingly intricate idle game that blends automation, strategy, and satisfying visual feedback into a relaxing yet engaging experience. At first glance, the concept appears simple—you begin with a small sapling and a basic loop of watering, harvesting, and selling fruit. But very quickly, the game reveals layers of depth through its building systems, quirky little worker creatures, and a progression loop that keeps unfolding the longer you play. What starts as a solitary tree soon evolves into a vibrant colony of scurrying units performing tasks, collecting resources, planting new crops, and optimizing production flows, all while you watch the system scale itself beyond your initial expectations. The core gameplay revolves around managing a continuously growing production system, where your goal is to accumulate wealth by automating the process of harvesting fruit and turning it into currency. While you can manually assist in the early game, the real satisfaction comes from setting up your colony to run efficiently on its own. Each element feeds into another—fruit is grown, collected, and processed in a giant wok, which generates income to be reinvested in upgrades, new buildings, and faster production chains. As your colony expands, new mechanics are introduced: automated planting, better pathfinding, advanced fruit types, and branching upgrade trees. These mechanics allow for increasing complexity without overwhelming the relaxing pace the game is built around. One of Idle Colony’s most distinctive qualities is how alive the world feels. The little workers, while simple in design, move about with purpose and charm. Watching them carry fruit, water saplings, and harvest trees is not just functional—it’s visually rewarding. The animations, though minimalist, give the entire colony a sense of bustling life. There’s something uniquely satisfying about watching all of your planning and upgrades culminate in a well-orchestrated loop of productivity. The AI behavior of these workers has improved over time with developer patches, though occasional hiccups remain. Some players have noted moments where workers loop inefficiently or get stuck, but these are minor annoyances rather than game-breaking flaws. Strategic planning plays a bigger role than the idle genre typically demands. Unlike games that rely solely on exponential numbers and passive accrual, Idle Colony encourages optimization through synergy between different upgrades, resource placement, and layout efficiency. Every decision feels like it has weight—whether you're choosing which upgrade path to invest in, reorganizing your fruit production zones, or deciding when to trigger the game’s prestige system. Prestige allows you to reset progress in exchange for long-term enhancements, adding replayability and incentive to dive deeper into each new run with better planning and broader goals. The progression curve feels well-paced, with a steady rollout of new features that keep the gameplay feeling fresh without overwhelming you with too many systems at once. Visually, the game is clean, bright, and inviting. The aesthetic is minimalist, with crisp edges and a focus on legibility and flow. The interface is functional, though at times it can feel cluttered when multiple menus or overlapping elements are on-screen. The design favors efficiency over flair, which works well for a game of this genre, but there’s still a certain whimsy in the animations and color choices that keeps the tone light and playful. The audio design is subtle, using light background ambiance and sound cues that fit well with the meditative nature of the gameplay, though it could benefit from more variety over extended sessions. Despite its strengths, Idle Colony isn’t without its quirks. Some players might find the tutorial insufficient for grasping the more advanced mechanics, especially when the systems start to scale up. The early game can also feel a bit slow for those used to more aggressive progression in idle games, though the pace is clearly intentional. There’s a clear emphasis on methodical building and refinement rather than mindless number inflation. Additionally, the prestige mechanic, while effective in concept, has been criticized for interrupting flow by taking players back to the main menu upon activation, breaking immersion at a pivotal moment. However, ongoing updates from the developer suggest a strong commitment to improvement, with community feedback often being implemented in meaningful ways. Idle Colony succeeds because it respects the player’s time while offering a gameplay loop that’s deeper than its surface suggests. It scratches the itch of watching numbers go up and systems click into place, but it also rewards thoughtfulness, patience, and creativity. The balance between automation and interaction is handled skillfully, making it a perfect game for both passive engagement and active optimization. Whether you're checking in for a few minutes at a time or diving in for longer sessions, there’s always something to tweak, upgrade, or improve. For fans of idle games looking for something with a bit more charm and strategy than the genre often provides, Idle Colony is a delightful and worthwhile experience. Rating: 8/10

对于增量游戏来说，毫无疑问的粪作，阴间的成就，墨迹的流程，恶心的轮回，可怜的数值，恶心的要命。不懂一个增量游戏为什么那么多限制，重来一把慢的要死，但是不重来就有天赋锁，真的恶心，而且没有任何可玩性，数值增长带来的反馈也几乎为0，玩了快400小时真的玩不下去了，这是我玩的所有挂机增量游戏里面最垃圾最恶心的，谁买谁后悔。 成就党也千万别买，蠢蠢找罪受，对糯米团子的低劣模仿罢了，真是又花钱又遭罪
比较早期的《糯米团子历代记》like增量游戏。 核心部分减去了单位规划系统，让本身玩法变得更专注于局外的天赋树联动而非局内规划资源（阶段性给予的选择升级还是有，但不再需要规划分配单位数量），开局的选择很大程度就决定了该波次推的上限，天赋树之间联动的深度也比较匮乏，局内少量操作可能可以算作更为idle的优点向，但我觉得是比较缺乏乐趣与吸引力的，不过鉴于“团子like”数量较少，尚可一试。
对于增量挂机游戏，除了视觉效果，轻松感，增量流畅度，策略体验，它们都能各个程度上地让这种机制简单的游戏变得好玩，虽说<奇果工坊>的策略深度算是及格，很多之前不懂的机制玩到后来发现原来都挺有意思，可是增益互斥的影响超过了流派的构筑性，不应该说"有难度会更好玩"，而是"这有点让我不够爽"——甚至后面几个成就都有点太令人发狂了，我应该没时间玩上这么久吧。

A visually interesting take on the idle/incremental game. Instead of very long-running continuous game improvement, Idle Colony is more about the individual "sessions" with different playstyle tactics to achieve the various goals of the game. Once reaching all the permanent upgrades, you basically get to chose various improvement options at will to try out various styles of gameplay for the each session. Instead of a single "best" path forward like many idler games, this one actually leaves you many options to accomplish the multiple achievements and completion of the game. My total playtime for full achievements could have definitely been improved drastically. For one example, I decided to push through one play session to go for the 'max fruit', and my build was not very well scaling beyond a certain point.
